learning.title: A curated file list is not a lane — path deletions are proven by the lane that owns the deleted path, run whole
learning.body:
dev-workflows on #518 (2026-11-17): five named test files passed and the report said "integration suites green" — but four tests in tests/integration/admit-a-compiled-plan-run-from-the-run-command_test.ts FAILED at the same head. That file runs only in the full integration lane, and CI skipped it (affected-route filter did not pull it in for the change set). The evidence was true about the five files and false as an impression of the lane.
Rule: for any change that DELETES a code path, the proof is the lane that owns the deleted path, run whole (pnpm test:integration or the equivalent), not a hand-picked list of files that touch the new code. CI's affected-route skip is a throughput tool, not a coverage claim; when CI skips a lane your change set did not "pull in" but your diff deletes behavior that lane pins, run it yourself and say so.
Corollary: phrase evidence claims at the scope you actually ran ("these five files pass") — never let a true statement about a subset read as a claim about the lane.
